title: Finite-diagonal Hom totalization of exact columns is acyclic
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,J,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site [def-pur-sheaf-hom] and let $E,A$ be cochain complexes of module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Suppose integers $N,M$ satisfy $E^p=0$ for $p>N$ and $A^q=0$ for $q<M$. For every pair of integers $p,q$, suppose the short complex $\mathcal Hom(E^p,A^{q-1})\to\mathcal Hom(E^p,A^q)\to\mathcal Hom(E^p,A^{q+1})$, with maps induced by $d_A$, is exact at its middle term. Then the total sheaf Hom complex $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,A)$ [def-pur-hom-complex] is acyclic [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules]. No freeness or separate acyclicity assumption is required.

source.place: Tag 0GM8 via Tag 0GM7, case (2); explicit finite-free Hom calculation

proof.text: Construct concretely the commuting bicomplex K in the opposite category with K^(p,q)=op Hom(E^p,A^(-q)), horizontal differential op of precomposition with d_E, and vertical differential op of postcomposition with d_A. Functoriality and d_E²=d_A²=0 prove the bicomplex identities. If E^p=0 then Hom(E^p,-)=0; if A^(-q)=0 then Hom(-,A^(-q))=0, so K is bounded above in its first index by N and uniformly in its second by -M. The finite-diagonal total exists.

Each column short complex is the opposite of the assumed exact internal-Hom short complex of A at -q; arithmetic identifies the adjacent negated indices. Hence every column of K is acyclic. Use the zero bicomplex Z and the zero map Z→K. Every column map is a quasi-isomorphism. The existing bounded-above columnwise total comparison therefore makes Tot(Z)→Tot(K) a quasi-isomorphism. Tot(Z) is zero, so Tot(K) is exact at every degree.

For each n, the signed opposite-total short-complex comparison identifies the Hom short complex at n with the unop of the total short complex at -n. Transport the exactness just proved through unop and this isomorphism. Thus the Hom complex is exact in every degree, hence acyclic.

proof_origin.description: V3 uses the already proved bounded-above bicomplex column comparison after passing to opposite module sheaves and negating the second index; only the product/differential short-complex identification remains as its own node. Unit route unchanged.
